qt: to the Commission Michalis Hadjipantela (PPE) Subject:

On 8 October 2026, Parliament adopted its resolution on the need for an EU strategy to counter Islamist entryism and the influence of the Muslim Brotherhood network. Parliament called on the Commission to provide a comprehensive overview of EU funds awarded to entities suspected of links to the network, to ensure the full traceability of funding down to the final beneficiary, and to make full use of the exclusion tools under the Financial Regulation1, including the Early Detection and Exclusion System. As the 2027 budgetary procedure is under way, it is essential that no EU funds, whether under direct, indirect or shared management, benefit individuals, associations or institutions affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood network or other extremist organisations, including those that act contrary to the values enshrined in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union. 1.
Can the Commission guarantee that no appropriations under the 2027 budget will be used to finance such individuals or entities?
What specific vetting and traceability measures will the Commission apply to applicants, partners and final beneficiaries under calls financed by the 2027 budget?

Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 September 2024 on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union (recast), (OJ L, 2024/2509, 26.9.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2509/oj). 1
